steps.statement: Why finite truncation gives an ALL-point scalar factorization.
steps.proof: Near each marked typeI point p, choose an actual local L-frame and a local uniformizer. Every section is t^(ord_p s_i) times a unit, whose absolute value is constant on a sufficiently small ball. Orders are nonnegative and some finite-weight section has order zero by basepoint freeness. The finitely many positive-order terms decay along the puncture ray, so the maximum is constant in that L-frame sufficiently far down it. The same applies to theta*. Consequently h=phi-theta* is constant on the whole tail BALL beyond one actual typeII point, not only on the ray. Truncate each of the finitely many marked rays beyond all switches. Then h factors at EVERY point through one ACTUAL finite skeleton Gamma_k containing Gamma0; typeI and typeIV points in every complementary open ball get the same attachment value. For weights in a fixed bounded range, choose the finitely many truncation points uniformly. Real-weight switching positions may be typeIII inside edges and must be retained. No USC argument or common-zero assertion from finitely many Shilov points replaces basepoint freeness.

This constructs an actual vertical Cartier bundle V with generic trivialization and degree deg(V|C_v)=P*Delta_out h(v), including both loop incidences. steps.statement: True trace on EVERY finite graph and the radial sign.
steps.proof: Let Gamma_j be ANY actual finite skeleton containing Gamma0. Enlarge to a common actual finite skeleton containing Gamma_j and the adapted carrier of phi, with all actual curvature breakpoints recorded as graph points. Outside Gamma_j this enlargement consists of attached finite trees because every cycle is already in Gamma0. Sum outgoing derivatives over each tree: internal incidences cancel pairwise, flat tails contribute zero, and the remaining boundary slope gives the tree's total TRUE curvature at its attachment. Since mu0 is supported on Gamma0, this proves Delta_Gamma_j(h|Gamma_j)=r_j*MA(phi)-mu0. On any tree away from Gamma0, the derivative of h in the direction away from the core equals minus the sum of all remaining TRUE MA masses on the future subtree. It is therefore nonpositive. The same statement holds on an interval before a typeIII atom. Every r_j(x) is an ancestor of x outside Gamma0, so h(r_jx)>=h(x) at EVERY point. Once Gamma_j contains the finite carrier of h, equality holds even at typeI/IV endpoints in complementary balls. Hence h(x)=inf_j h(r_jx) ALL-point. This trace/radial statement uses actual weighted FS curvature, not abstract PA with arbitrary signs.
